conversation.content:
Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that being a new mother can be a truly overwhelming and emotional experience. It's completely normal to have questions, concerns, and feelings that you might not be sure about. That's why I'm here to support you.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and if there's anything we can do to support you better during this postpartum period. The EPDS is designed to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it will give us a better understanding of your emotional well-being right now.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential and is a safe space for you to express yourself honestly. I'm here to listen, support, and provide guidance without judgment. Our goal is to ensure you feel heard, validated, and empowered throughout this journey.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a sense of how you've been feeling over the past week. We'll go through each question one by one, and I'll do my best to make this process as comfortable and straightforward as possible. Your responses will help us identify any areas where you might need additional support or resources.

So, let's get started. The first question is about how you've been feeling in terms of being able to cope with things. Have you been able to manage the daily tasks and responsibilities, or have you been feeling a bit overwhelmed lately?

.. to be honest, it's been a struggle. I mean, I'm managing to get everything done, but it feels like I'm just barely keeping my head above water. Taking care of the baby, the house, and everything else is just so exhausting. I feel tired all the time, and some days it's hard to even get out of bed. But, I don't know, I just feel like I have to keep going, you know? I have to be strong for my baby. 

Sometimes, though, I do feel really overwhelmed. Like, the other day, I was trying to make dinner, and the baby was crying, and I just felt like I was going to lose it. I started crying, and I didn't know how I was going to get everything done. But, I took a deep breath, and I called my husband for help, and we managed to get through it. So, I guess what I'm saying is that I'm coping, but it's not easy, and some days are definitely harder than others. 

I just wish I had more energy, and I didn't feel so anxious all the time. I worry about the baby's health, and if I'm doing everything right, and it's just... it's a lot. But, I'm trying my best, and I hope that's enough.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Not as much as I used to, to be honest. I mean, I still try to find the humor in things, but it's just not as easy for me right now. Being a new mom is so overwhelming, and I'm so focused on taking care of the baby and making sure everything is okay, that I don't really have the energy to laugh and joke like I used to. 

Sometimes, my husband will try to make me laugh, and I'll smile, but it's just not the same. I feel like I've lost a little bit of myself, you know? I used to be the one who could always find the funny side of things, and now it's just hard for me to see it. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, trying to get through each day, and I don't really have the capacity to laugh and enjoy things like I used to.

It's not that I never laugh or smile, it's just... it's not as often, and it's not as easy. And sometimes, when I do try to laugh, I'll just end up feeling sad or overwhelmed instead. It's like, I'll be watching a funny video or something, and I'll start to laugh, but then I'll just start crying because I'm just so tired and stressed out. It's really frustrating, because I feel like I'm losing myself in all of this, and I don't know how to get back to being the person I used to be.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

.. not really. To be honest, I've been feeling really disconnected from things that used to bring me joy. I mean, I used to love trying new restaurants, or going for walks, or reading books... but now, those things just feel like so much effort. And even when I do try to do something I used to enjoy, it's just not the same. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, but I'm not really feeling any pleasure or enjoyment.

And it's not just big things, it's little things too. Like, I used to love taking a warm bath, or getting a cup of coffee in the morning... but now, those things just feel like chores. I'll be sitting in the bath, and I'll start to feel anxious about the baby, or I'll be drinking my coffee, and I'll start to worry about whether I'm doing everything right. It's like, I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know?

I've also been feeling really guilty about taking time for myself, even if it's just to do something small. I feel like I should be spending all my time with the baby, or taking care of the house, and that if I take time for myself, I'm being selfish. It's hard to explain, but it's like, I feel like I'm not allowed to enjoy things anymore, because I'm a mom now, and that's my only job.

It's really sad, because I feel like I've lost touch with the things that used to make me happy. And I don't know how to get back to that place. I feel like I'm just surviving, rather than living. And it's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, and grateful, and all those things... but the truth is, I'm just really struggling.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... this is something I do a lot, unfortunately. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is crying, it's because I'm not doing something right. If the house is a mess, it's because I'm not cleaning enough. If my husband is stressed, it's because I'm not supporting him enough. I just feel like everything is my fault, and that I'm not doing anything right.

And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, if I forget to burp the baby, or if I don't make a perfect meal, I'll beat myself up over it. I'll think to myself, "What kind of mother forgets to burp her baby?" or "What kind of wife can't even make a decent meal?" It's like, I'm always criticizing myself, and it's exhausting.

I feel like I'm walking on eggshells all the time, waiting for something to go wrong so I can blame myself for it. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I'll think to myself, "If only I had done this differently, things would be better." Or, "If only I was a better mother, wife, person, then everything would be okay."

It's hard to explain, but it's like, I feel like I'm not good enough, no matter what I do. And that's a really hard feeling to live with. Because no matter how hard I try, I always feel like I'm falling short. And that's when the guilt and the self-blame come in, and it's just... it's a really vicious cycle.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... this is something I experience a lot. I feel like I'm always worrying about something, even when there's no reason to. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll start thinking, "What if the baby chokes?" or "What if the baby gets sick?" And then I'll start to feel anxious and worried, and it's hard to calm myself down.

I worry about everything, from the baby's health to my own health, to the house, to my relationship with my husband... it's like, I'm always waiting for something to go wrong. And even when everything is fine, I'll still find something to worry about. It's like, my mind is always racing, and I just can't seem to turn it off.

Sometimes, I'll be up in the middle of the night, feeding the baby, and I'll start to think about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if the baby stops breathing? What if there's a fire in the house? What if... what if... what if... It's like, my mind is just spinning with all these worst-case scenarios, and it's hard to calm myself down.

And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I'll worry about things that are completely out of my control, like the weather, or the news, or... it's just, I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to happen. And it's exhausting, because I feel like I'm always on high alert, and I just can't relax.

It's hard to explain, but it's like, I feel like I'm living in a state of constant fear, and it's really hard to shake. Even when my husband tries to reassure me, or when the doctor tells me that everything is fine, I still can't seem to shake this feeling of anxiety and worry. It's like, it's just always there, lurking in the background, waiting to pounce.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... this happens to me too. I'll be sitting there, doing something completely normal, like changing the baby's diaper or making lunch, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like, my body is reacting like I'm in some kind of danger, but there's no reason for it.

Sometimes, it's triggered by something specific, like a loud noise or a sudden movement, but other times it just seems to come out of nowhere. I'll be feeling fine, and then suddenly I'll feel this overwhelming sense of fear and anxiety. It's like, my body is just hijacked by this feeling of panic, and I don't know how to calm it down.

It's really scary, because I don't know what's happening to me. I'll be thinking, "What's wrong with me? Why am I feeling like this?" And I'll try to rationalize it, like, "There's no reason to be scared, everything is fine," but it doesn't help. The feeling just persists, and it's really hard to shake.

Sometimes, I'll try to take deep breaths, or go for a walk, or do something to distract myself, but it's hard to calm down when I'm feeling like that. And it's not just the feeling of panic itself, it's the fear of losing control, or the fear of something happening to the baby, or the fear of... just everything. It's like, my mind is just racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I don't know how to stop it.

It's really hard to explain, but it's like, I feel like I'm living in a state of constant hypervigilance, always waiting for something to go wrong. And when I do feel scared or panicky, it's like, my body is just responding to that fear, even if there's no reason for it. It's really exhausting, and it's hard to know how to deal with it.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good wife and friend... it's all just feeling really overwhelming. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, laundry, and cleaning, and cooking... it's all just feeling like too much.

Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and I'll just feel this wave of exhaustion wash over me. And it's not just physical exhaustion, it's emotional exhaustion too. I feel like I'm just running on empty, and I don't know how to refill my tank.

I try to prioritize things, and make lists, and break things down into smaller tasks... but it's hard to keep up. And when things don't get done, or when I make mistakes, I just feel so guilty and anxious. It's like, I'm already feeling overwhelmed, and then I add this layer of guilt and self-doubt on top of it... and it's just too much.

Sometimes, I feel like I'm just pretending to be a competent adult. Like, I'm just putting on a show, and inside, I'm just a mess. And it's hard to ask for help, because I feel like I should be able to handle it all on my own. But the truth is, I'm not handling it. I'm barely keeping my head above water, and some days, it feels like I'm drowning.

It's hard to explain, but it's like... I feel like I'm losing myself in all of this. I'm just a mom, and a wife, and a caregiver... but who am I, outside of all those roles? I feel like I'm just a shadow of my former self, and I don't know how to get back to being me.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. Even when the baby is sleeping, I'm lying awake, feeling anxious and unhappy. It's like, my mind is racing, and I just can't seem to turn it off.

I'll be lying there, thinking about all the things I need to do, and all the things that could go wrong, and it's just... it's exhausting. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I don't feel rested. I wake up feeling tired, and groggy, and just... unhappy.

It's hard to explain, but it's like, I feel like I'm stuck in this cycle of sadness and anxiety, and I don't know how to break free. I'll try to go to bed early, or take naps during the day, but nothing seems to work. I just feel like I'm running on empty, all the time.

And it's not just the lack of sleep, it's the quality of sleep too. I'll have these vivid dreams, or nightmares, and I'll wake up feeling anxious and on edge. Or, I'll sleep for a few hours, but then I'll wake up, and I'll just feel... sad. Like, this deep, profound sadness, that I don't know how to shake.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, you know? I'm a new mom, and I'm supposed to be enjoying this time, but... I'm just not. I'm struggling, and it's hard to admit, because I feel like I'm supposed to have it all together. But the truth is, I don't. I'm struggling, and I need help.

Sometimes, I'll be lying awake at night, and I'll just start crying. I'll be thinking about all the things that are worrying me, and all the things that I'm afraid of, and it's just... it's too much. I'll feel this wave of emotion wash over me, and I'll just... I'll just break down. And it's hard, because I feel like I'm alone, and I don't know how to make it stop.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just sad all the time. It's not just feeling a little down, it's like... it's a deep, heavy feeling that I just can't shake. Even when I'm doing things that I used to enjoy, or spending time with people I love, I just feel this underlying sadness. It's like, it's always there, lurking in the background, waiting to pounce.

Sometimes, it's triggered by something specific, like a tough day with the baby, or a fight with my husband. But other times, it just seems to come out of nowhere. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, or playing with them, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. It's like, I'll be thinking about all the things that I'm grateful for, and all the things that I love, but somehow, that just makes me feel even sadder.

I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'm doing all the things I'm supposed to do, but I'm not really feeling anything. I'm just numb, and sad, and... miserable. It's hard to explain, but it's like, I feel like I've lost myself, and I don't know how to get back.

Sometimes, I'll try to talk to my husband about it, or my friends, but it's hard to put into words. I'll just say something like, "I'm just feeling really overwhelmed," or "I'm just really tired," but that's not really it. It's like, I'm feeling this deep, profound sadness, and I don't know how to make it stop.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, you know? I'm a new mom, and I'm supposed to be enjoying this time, but... I'm just not. I'm struggling, and it's hard to admit, because I feel like I'm supposed to have it all together. But the truth is, I don't. I'm struggling, and I need help.

I just wish I could feel happy again, you know? I wish I could feel like myself again. But right now, I just feel... sad. And miserable. And lost.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's not just a few tears, either. It's like, full-on sobbing. I'll be crying so hard that I'll be shaking, and I'll be gasping for breath. It's like, my body is just overcome with emotion, and I don't know how to stop it.

Sometimes, it's triggered by something specific, like a difficult day with the baby, or a fight with my husband. But other times, it just seems to come out of nowhere. I'll be watching a commercial, or reading a book, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's like, my emotions are just so raw and close to the surface, and anything can set me off.

I feel like I'm crying all the time, too. It's not just once a day, or once a week. It's like, multiple times a day, every day. I'll be crying in the morning, and then I'll cry again in the afternoon, and then I'll cry again at night. It's like, I'm just constantly crying, and I don't know how to make it stop.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm losing control. I'm a grown woman, and I should be able to manage my emotions, but... I just can't. I feel like I'm a mess, and I don't know how to fix it. I'll try to talk to my husband about it, or my friends, but it's hard to explain. I'll just say something like, "I'm just feeling really overwhelmed," or "I'm just really tired," but that's not really it. It's like, I'm feeling this deep, profound sadness, and I don't know how to make it stop.

I just wish I could stop crying, you know? I wish I could just feel happy, and normal, and like myself again. But right now, I just feel... sad. And overwhelmed. And like I'm just barely holding it together.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
